newsitem.title: CHINA: China hails talks aimed at Korea peace treaty.
newsitem.headline: China hails talks aimed at Korea peace treaty.

text.p: China said on Wednesday it supported efforts to create a peace mechanism for the Korean peninsula and welcomed proposed four-party talks.

"We approve of establishing a peace mechanism for the Korean peninsula and take a positive attitude toward the four-party talks," the official Xinhua news agency quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang as saying.
China had agreed to join the talks and would take a constructive role in efforts to create a peace mechanism to bring long-term peace and stability to the Korean peninsula, Tang said.

North and South Korea as well as China and the United States -- the four main parties in the 1950-53 Korean War -- plan to meet in New York in August to decide on an agenda and other procedural details for formal peace talks.
China backed North Korea in the Korean conflict against the South and U.S.-led United Nations forces.
The famine-hit North on Monday agreed to attend the talks aimed at reaching a peace treaty to replace the armistice that ended the conflict but left the North and South technically still at war.
Until this week, Pyongyang had held out for major food aid as a condition for attending the talks.
Flooding devastated North Korea's rice crop in 1995 and 1996, and international aid officials have warned that the isolated Stalinist state was facing famine.
